title: P1: active Work Item dirty synchronization
outOfScope: Rewriting archived #691/#699 Contract, Summary, Outcome, closure, PR, or branch evidence.
Rebasing, committing, stashing, pushing, or archiving #663 while the corrective protocol is unavailable.
Provider-side mutation from the synchronization command.
Relaxing ownership, conflict, stale-evidence, or unsafe-state rejection.

sources.reason: Current synchronization implementation rejects a dirty active Work Item before it can rebase.
Authoritative corrective requirement derived from #663's current-main synchronization deadlock.
Immutable predecessor evidence for the original synchronization capability; it must not be rewritten.

riskAssessment.reason: A synchronization transition changes the branch and evidence basis of an active Work Item; it must preserve explicit authority, provenance, conflict safety, and verification invalidation.

reasons: Work Item synchronization changes governed lifecycle and evidence-binding behavior.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized automatic corrective execution; the Contract bounds the synchronization transaction and its fail-closed tests.

preReviewWarnings: A synchronization checkpoint must be explicit and evidence-bound, never a hidden temporary commit or stash.
A failed conflict or ownership check must leave the active Work Item recoverable and not falsely synchronized.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: An eligible dirty active Work Item can create a governed synchronization checkpoint and transition to the verified latest remote default base without a manual rebase, temporary commit, or stash.
The transition records old/new base, exact task/branch/head/Contract/Summary bindings, checkpoint identity, invalidated verification, and a recoverable receipt.

The command rejects unowned or ambiguous changes, wrong branch, archived Work Item, unrelated dirty paths, provider mutation, invalid remote/base identity, and rebase conflict without claiming synchronization.
Only a Contract explicitly authorizing the synchronization checkpoint may invoke it; the checkpoint is a first-class lifecycle record rather than an implicit workaround.
Source and installed-template entrypoints, documentation, and generated capability/documentation-alignment evidence remain in parity.
Executable tests reproduce the #663 sequence and all unsafe-state rejections.
guidelines: A synchronization checkpoint must be explicit, deterministic, and bound to active Work Item evidence.
Do not permit manual rebase, hidden temporary state, provider mutation, or archive rewrite as a synchronization substitute.
Reject every incomplete, ambiguous, conflicting, or stale lifecycle state before modifying Git state.
Keep source and installed-template command behavior and documentation aligned.

intent.problem: #663 cannot reconcile to current main after #697 because ai-synchronize-work-item correctly rejects a dirty active Work Item, while the existing lifecycle offers no legal way to make its unarchived implementation clean. This produces a deadlock and invites prohibited manual rebase, stash, or temporary-commit workarounds.
constraints: Limit the transition to local Git state.
Record the checkpoint and invalidate stale verification.
Retain a recoverable active Work Item on every failure.
Use the user's standing mandate only for this bounded repository-governance operation.
intent.rationale: A first-class, receipt-bound synchronization checkpoint turns the unavoidable pre-archive clean-state requirement into an auditable lifecycle transition. It is not a hidden temporary commit because it is deliberately authorized, recorded, and becomes the rebased active Work Item history.

rawUserRequest: Execute the complete remediation plan automatically; if a process problem is encountered, create a corrective Work Item first and do not use a temporary workaround. Use parallelism only when safe. Require explicit Outcome traffic lights.

declaredIntent.summary: Repair the active dirty Work Item synchronization deadlock revealed by #663 without weakening governance or mutating immutable predecessor evidence.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: The user authorized automatic execution and required corrective Work Items for process defects.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A dirty eligible active Work Item with only declared owned changes synchronizes to a newer verified remote base.
scenarioCoverage.expected: A receipt records the explicit checkpoint and old/new base; the Work Item remains active and prior verification is invalidated.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: An isolated Git fixture exercises the complete #663-style sequence.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: An active Work Item has an unowned path, wrong branch, archived state, invalid remote/base, or a rebase conflict.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The command fails closed without synchronization, provider mutation, or loss of recoverable active evidence.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Focused boundary tests assert rejection and unchanged fixture state.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: An installed adopter invokes the same documented synchronization command.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The installed Make entrypoint retains source-equivalent argument and receipt behavior.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Installed-runtime parity regression executes the command surface.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff and restore related tests and docs.
